x: Commentary on the Surah “When the Sky Is Split Open” (al-Inshiqaq). In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

The discussion of the interpretation of the words of the Exalted: “When the sky is split open (1), and heeds its Lord and is bound to do so (2); and when the earth is spread out (3), casts out what is within it and empties itself (4), and heeds its Lord and is bound to do so (5).”
He, Exalted is He, says: When the sky is torn apart and split, so that it becomes openings.
His words: “and heeds its Lord and is bound to do so.”

The heavens, as they are torn apart and split open, listen to their Lord and obey His command to them. In Arabic, they say, “He gave you permission in this matter,” meaning, “he listened to you.” From this comes the report related from the Prophet, God’s blessings and peace be upon him: “God does not listen to anything as He listens to a prophet reciting the Qur’an melodiously.”
By this he meant: “God does not listen to anything as He listens to a prophet reciting the Qur’an melodiously”
n
. Also from this usage is the poet’s statement
n

: “They are deaf when they hear good things said of me … but when I am mentioned with evil before them, they listen.” The basic expression used by the Arabs for obedience is “he listened to him,” from the sense of listening. One says, “I listened to you,” meaning, “I heard what you said and obeyed what you said and commanded.”
The interpreters held views similar to what we have said concerning the meaning of His words, “and heeds its Lord.”

of the apodosis of His words, “When the sky is split open,” and His words, “and when the earth is spread out.”

Some of the grammarians of Basra said that “When the sky is split open” is connected to the meaning of His words, “O human being, you are laboring toward your Lord with great exertion, and you will meet Him,” with the order of the words advanced and delayed.
Some of the grammarians of Kufa

said: One of the exegetes stated that the apodosis of “When the sky is split open” is His words, “and it heeds.” He [the grammarian] said: We consider this to be an opinion the exegete arrived at, likening it to God’s words, “until, when they come to it and its gates are opened” [al-Zumar 39:73]. For we have not heard an apodosis introduced by the conjunction
i
wa
after an opening “when,” with no preceding clause; nor have we heard this in a sentence beginning with “when.” Rather, the Arabs use
i
wa

in the expression “until, when it happened,” and “when it happened…” They do not go beyond that. He said: The apodosis in “When the sky is split open” and “when the earth is spread out” is as though it were omitted, because the meaning is known and has appeared repeatedly in the Qur’an, so it is understood. Alternatively, its apodosis could be “O human being,” as when someone says: “When such-and-such happens, O people, you will see what you have done, whether good or evil.”

in it. The apodosis of “When the sky is split open” has also been explained in terms of the reward and punishment a person will encounter, so that the meaning is: You will see the reward and punishment when the sky is split open. Our correct view is that its apodosis is omitted, because the addressees understand its meaning. The meaning of the statement is: When the sky is split open, a person will see what he sent ahead, whether good or evil. This is clarified by His words: “O human being, you are laboring toward your Lord with great exertion, and you will meet Him,” and the verses that follow.
The discussion of the interpretation of the words of the Exalted: “O human being, you are laboring toward your Lord with great exertion, and you will meet Him (6).

As for the one who is given his record in his right hand (7), he will be called to account with an easy reckoning (8), and will return to his family rejoicing (9).” He, Exalted is He, says: O human being, you are doing deeds for your Lord, and you will meet Him with those deeds, whether they are good or evil. He says: Let your deeds, then, be among those that save you from His displeasure and bring you His approval; do not let them be among those that incur His displeasure against you and cause you to perish.
The interpreters held views similar to what we have said.

That is the reckoning in the manner we have described, and for that reason it is called “being called to account.”

, because the interpretations of all the exegetes have been transmitted in accordance with that reading, even though the other readings have understandable interpretations. Since the correct reading is what we have mentioned, the correct interpretation is that you, Muhammad, will surely pass from one condition to another, and from one hardship to another. Although the address is directed to the Messenger of God, God’s blessings and peace be upon him, all people are intended: they will encounter successive conditions amid the hardships and terrors of the Day of Resurrection. We have said this because the speech before the words “you will surely pass from one state to another” is addressed to everyone, and so is the speech after it. It is therefore more fitting that this verse follow what comes before and after it.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in how they read it.
‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Mas‘ud and his companions, Ibn ‘Abbas, and most reciters of Mecca and Kufa read it *la-tarkabanna*, with the ta’ and ba’ carrying fathahs (3).
Those who read it this way also differed concerning its meaning.
Others who held this interpretation and read it in this way said that what is meant is: “You, Muhammad, will surely ascend from one heaven to another.”

Others who read this reading said that what is meant is that the sky will undergo different kinds of transformation: it will split apart with clouds at one time, turn red at another, become like a rose-colored oil, and at another time become like molten metal.

Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas‘udi narrated to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, who said: ‘Abd Allah read this word, “you will surely pass from one state to another,” and said: “The sky: from one condition to another, and from one station to another.”
Mihran also related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Famuah, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas‘ud, that he read it *la-tarkabanna* with the ba’ in the accusative, and said: “It is the sky” (3).

Most of the reciters of Medina and some of the reciters of Kufa read it *la-tarkabunna*, with the ta’ and a dammah on the ba’, as an address to all people (1), meaning that they will pass through states of hardship, one after another.
Some have also mentioned that it was read with a ya’ and a dammah on the ba’ (2)(3)(4), as a statement about all people, that they will do so.

In my view, the most correct reading is that of those who read it with the ta’ and a fathah on the ba’ (5), because the interpretations of all the exegetes have been transmitted in accordance with that reading, even though the other readings have understandable interpretations.
Since the correct reading is what we have mentioned, the correct interpretation is that you, Muhammad, will surely pass from one condition to another, and from one hardship to another.

So give them news of a painful punishment (24), except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; they shall have a reward that will not be cut off (25).”
His words: “Rather, those who disbelieve call it a lie.” He, Exalted is He, says: Rather, those who disbelieve call God’s signs and His revelation lies.

His words: “and God knows best what they conceal within themselves.” He, Exalted is He, says: God knows best the denial of God’s Book and His Messenger that these polytheists conceal in their breasts.

c: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said
m: concerning His words, “and God knows best what they conceal within themselves”: “A person stores his belongings and wealth—this in one place, that in another. In the same way, God knows what they store of deeds. The evil deeds are among the things their hearts contain; good and evil deeds gather within them. Hearts are the containers of all these deeds, good and evil. He knows what they conceal and what they disclose. He has indeed stored up for you something of which no one knows what it is, from the Qur’an and other matters. So fear God, and beware lest you introduce some of this filth into the noble deeds, thereby corrupting them.”

x: His words: “So give them news of a painful punishment.” Glorious is His remembrance: So, Muhammad, give these people who reject God’s signs the news of a painful punishment from God, one that will cause them pain. “Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds”: He says: Except for those among them who repent, believe, and acknowledge His oneness, the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad, God’s blessings and peace be upon him, and resurrection after death; “and do righteous deeds”: that is, they perform the obligations God has imposed and refrain from committing what God has forbidden them to commit.

His words: “they shall have a reward that will not be cut off.” He, Exalted is He, says: These people who believed and performed righteous deeds will have a reward that is neither reckoned nor diminished.
The interpreters held views similar to what we have said.

notes.en: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, and Yaʿqūb read it this way. Al-Nashr, 2/298.
notes.ar: وبها قرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب. ينظر النشر 2/ 298.

notes.en: He is al-Farrāʾ, in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān, 3/252.
notes.ar: هو الفراء في معاني القرآن 3/ 252.

notes.en: The manuscripts read “he recited”; context requires the adopted reading.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "قرأ". والمثبت ما يقتضيه السياق

notes.en: This reading is attributed to ʿUmar, but is anomalous. Al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 8/448.
notes.ar: وهذه القراءة عن عمر، وهى شاذة. البحر المحيط 8/ 448.

notes.en: All readings are correct.
notes.ar: القراءات كلها صواب.

notes.en: S, T1, T2, and T3 read “the polytheists.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت،2، ت 3: "المشركون".
